note: Track note-names (theory-basics), step 2: sharps and flats, as the black key beside a white one, then one sharp (F♯ in G) and one flat (B♭ in F) on the staff. Missing: piano-keys labels only the notes of its scale, so the black keys carry no names, and no tool shows one black key under both of its names.

exercise.title: Sharps and flats
exercise.why: A sharp is the next key to the right on the piano and a flat is the next key to the left, so every black key gets its name from the white key beside it.

cells.text:
On the piano below, tap {{c}}, then the black key just to its right: that is {{c-sharp}}, a half step higher. Now tap {{d}}, then the same black key: from this side it is {{d-flat}}, a half step lower.
Go along the other black keys the same way, and say both names of each.

The staff below shows G major, a scale that needs one sharp. Tap up from {{1}} and say each letter: the ringed note is {{f-sharp}}, not F.
Then tap {{f-sharp}} and the {{1}} above it: they are a half step apart.

This staff shows F major, a scale that needs one flat. Tap up from {{1}} and say each letter: the ringed note is {{b-flat}}, not B.
Then tap {{3}} and {{b-flat}}: they are a half step apart too.
